title: Candidate contextual-problem playbook and handoff protocol
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for using 'contextual problems' (small, realistic tasks seeded with product context) as part of our interview loop and the downstream handoff into the first 14 days of onboarding. Goal is twofold: 1) get closer to role signal (not whiteboard) and 2) reduce time-to-value for new hires by creating an explicit handoff artifact that product/eng can pick up after an offer.

Scope and when to use:
- Use for mid-senior IC roles (IC3+) across infra, platform, and serving-runtime teams as an experiment (pilot cohort Q2 2025).
- Not for leadership hires or pure research roles.
- Replace one take-home + one system-design panel with a contextual problem + a short pairing session.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Candidate receives a 2-hour contextual problem: a concise repo snapshot (fake data, simplified infra) + 3 focused questions.
- Candidate does up to 4 hours asynchronous work (can be split) and submits a one-page README + 6–10 line patch or scripts.
- Interview loop includes a 30–40 min pairing review with an interviewer who graded with the rubric; rubric + artifact become the onboarding 'starter ticket' if hired.

Design principles:
- Keep scope shallow: isomorphic to a real tiny shard of our stack but self-contained. Avoid costly infra setup.
- Use sandboxed repos (no secrets); deterministic seed data.
- Evaluate problem-solving, tradeoffs, safety/edge-case thought, and code clarity. Not focused on full production polish.
- Turn interview artifact into an onboarding starter ticket: includes context, candidate notes, and suggested first micro-task for week 1.

Candidate-facing instructions (template):
- "We want to see how you approach a realistic, small task related to Redwood's serving runtime. You have up to 4 hours total; do what you can. Deliverables: a 1-page README (what you did, tradeoffs, open questions) and a single patch or script. We will review with you for 30–40 minutes in a pairing session. No need to deploy anywhere. We value clarity more than completeness."
- Include a short rubric summary they see ahead: clarity, edge-cases, engineering judgment, tradeoffs, testing approach.

Contextual problem structure (authors: eng + product):
- Short background (3–6 sentences) explaining why this matters.
- Minimal code snapshot (100–300 LOC) with a clear failure case to fix or feature to add.
- Small dataset or generator; clear instructions to run locally.
- 3 guiding questions (e.g., "How would you avoid cache-stomping?", "What metrics would you expect to track?").

Rubric (interviewer fills):
- 0–3 scale for each axis (0 = missing, 1 = partial, 2 = solid, 3 = standout)
  - Problem framing & clarity (how candidate scoped problem)
  - Tradeoff reasoning (why design choices)
  - Correctness & edge-case thinking (tests, failure modes)
  - Code clarity & incremental PR sense (simpler patch with good docs > huge incomplete change)
  - Pairing communication (during review — clarity, acceptance of feedback)
  - Onboarding readiness signal (how fast they could be productive week 1)
- Overall recommend: hire / no-hire / neutral with reasons.

Interview rotation suggestion (example 3-interviewer loop):
- Async reviewer (engineer): quick run of tests, look at README, score tradeoffs.
- Pairing reviewer (senior eng): 30–40 min pairing session to discuss approach and iterate.
- Hiring manager / product partner: 20–30 min to assess alignment to roadmap and cross-team signals.

Scoring weight guidance (internal):
- Tradeoffs & reasoning: 30%
- Correctness & edge-cases: 25%
- Code clarity & PR hygiene: 20%
- Pairing communication: 15%
- Onboarding readiness: 10%

Handoff protocol (if candidate is hired):
- Interviewer must export the rubric + submitted artifacts into the canned starter-ticket template (see below) within 48 hours of offer acceptance.
- Starter-ticket template fields (flattened into JIRA/Asana fields): context paragraph; link to artifact (repo snapshot); candidate README summary; suggested week-1 micro-task; list of unanswered questions; owner in eng for onboarding.
- People Ops creates onboarding kick-off with owner and attaches starter-ticket to new-hire plan.

Starter-ticket template (copy/paste ready):
- Title: "Starter: [candidate-lastname] - contextual-problem: [short task]"
- Description: 2–3 sentence context + paste candidate README summary.
- Artifact: link to archived repo snapshot (zip) + diff.
- Week 1 micro-task: e.g., "Run local harness, add a small integration test for X, and document expected metrics."
- Open questions: bullet list from rubric notes.
- Suggested reviewers: names from interview panel.

14-day onboarding checklist (for eng owner):
- Day 0: unzip artifact into staging workspace; confirm run instructions work.
- Day 1: pair 1:1 to walk through candidate's README and decisions (30m).
- Day 3: assign week-1 micro-task from starter-ticket; set acceptance criteria.
- Day 7: short demo + written notes on what changed; add tests if missing.
- Day 14: retrospective with new hire — what helped, what was confusing, any missing context to add to starter-ticket.

Quality controls & safety:
- Keep candidate data synthetic and scrubbed. No live customer logs.
- Problem authors must have at least one peer review from a different subteam to avoid knowledge leak.
- Rotate problem bank quarterly; archive used prompts and tag by team and skill.

Operational notes (checklist to run pilot):
- Create 8 sandbox problems across platform/serving/runtime with owners (lee, omar, priya).
- Add problem bank entry in Confluence + link to zipped repo listings.
- Update ATS template to accept one-page README + artifact zip.
- Train 12 interviewers on rubric (2hr calibration session).
- Track time-to-offer and first-30-day performance for hires from this loop vs baseline.

Open questions / to resolve:
- Compensation for candidates doing async work (still debating paid take-homes vs shorter async tasks).
- How to quantify onboarding-readiness metric consistently across teams.
- Should we give candidates sample telemetry output to reason about metrics? pros/cons.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep docs lean; interviewers keep comments inline in rubric sheet.
- Slack thread for pilot: #people-ops-contextual-pilot.
- Jira epic: HR-3421 (pilot tracking).
